architectural_decisions.decision: Keep the public UrlService(UrlRepository) constructor, annotate it with @org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired, and delegate to this(repository, java.time.Clock.systemUTC()). Add public UrlService(UrlRepository, java.time.Clock), store a private final Clock, and use java.time.Instant.now(clock) for both creation validation and redirect expiration checks. Use fixed UTC in additive GeneratedExpirationBoundaryTest; existing tests and build remain unchanged.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Deterministic equality-boundary testing without altering HTTP 201/400/404/410, optional expiration, redirects, or click behavior.

ambiguities.question: Should the URL expiration be fixed at 24 hours from link creation, or should each caller provide a future UTC expiration timestamp?

context.requirement: Enhance the existing URL shortener with optional URL expiration. Preserve existing links, HTTP 410 for expired URLs, and existing active-link redirect behavior. There is exactly one deliberately unresolved configuration decision for this demonstration: use a fixed 24-hour TTL computed from link creation, OR let each caller provide a future UTC expiration timestamp. Neither mode is approved yet. Ask the human to choose between those two modes before codebase analysis or planning. Do not select the suggested default automatically. No code changes may execute until the later engineering plan approval.

Replace both creation and access Instant.now() calls with Instant.now(clock). Preserve strictly-future optional caller-provided UTC expiration and HTTP 400 for past/equal-now; preserve null expiration, HTTP 201/404/410, redirects and clicks. Controller/entity behavior already exists and needs no edit. Existing integration tests are read-only coverage references. The separately approved additive test stage renders future/past/equal-now/missing assertions with a fixed UTC clock; no existing tests/build modifications.
